name: Electric Motorized Bicycle
description: An electric motorized bicycle, or electric bicycle: a two-wheeled vehicle propelled by human power, an electric motor rated at no more than 2 horsepower, or both, with a top speed of 28 mph, in one of three classes. Defined by Rhode Island General Laws §31-1-3(g), with the classes, state-property use and helmet rule added as chapter 31-19.7 by H 7713A / S 2829A (2024).
restrictions: Two wheels, with an electric motor rated at no more than 2 SAE horsepower (about 1,492 W) and a top speed of 28 mph
Class 1 assists only while the rider pedals and stops assisting at 20 mph
Class 2 has a throttle-actuated motor that stops assisting at 20 mph
Class 3 assists only while the rider pedals and stops assisting at 28 mph
Riders and passengers under 21 must wear a CPSC-compliant helmet, on any class
Not a motor vehicle: no driver's license or registration
Has the rights and duties of a vehicle driver on the road, and may ride on highway shoulders except where bicycles are barred
Only Class 1 is allowed on state bicycle trails and paths
The Department of Environmental Management decides by regulation where e-bikes may ride on the parks and other properties it manages
Banned from sidewalks and crosswalks in New Shoreham (Block Island)
One faster than 28 mph or with a motor over 2 horsepower is a motor vehicle, not an electric motorized bicycle, and needs a license and registration
